correctness.rationale: For connected simple graph over R with adjacency A of nullity 1, an isomorphism P from graph evolution algebra A to random-walk evolution algebra D^(−1)A has p_i∘p_j in kernel of (D^(−1)A)^T=D ker A for every i≠j. A generator z of ker A cannot be singleton supported. If |supp z|>=3, overlapping columns would confine all rows on supp z to rank <=2, contradicting invertible P; hence monomial. If |supp z|=2, binary nonzero adjacency rows force one unique false-twin pair, and pairwise orthogonality forces at most one 2x2 block. The twin rows image square equality and a common neighbor square imply the block has equal row/column sums, and real orthogonality then forces diagonal or swapped scalar form. Monomial coefficient comparison proves underlying permutation is graph automorphism; neighbor scalings are constant on even-walk classes, forcing regular or bipartite biregular degrees. Explicit positive diagonal scalings prove both converses. In K1,3 adjacency nullity 2, real rotations of the three-leaf subspace fixing its sum give nonmonomial automorphisms, making threshold sharp. Independent exact graph rank/twin/kernel census checked 439 connected graphs of sizes 3..5 including 259 twin cases. Uniform proof uses linear algebra, not census.
residual_risks: The independent finite checks are bounded and do not themselves establish infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Cadavid–Rodiño Montoya–Rodríguez (arXiv:1710.10516) settle nonsingular graphs and conjecture singular; 2024 Cadavid et al study individual singular families; 2025 Rodiño et al show 2LI/twin-free monomial criteria, which covers only the twin-free ingredient. October 2026 survey lists singular graph/RW isomorphism as open. Neither inspected primary theorem classifies all corank-one connected simple graphs including the unique false-twin pair, and the rank-2x2 block argument is a genuine additional reduction. Historical possibility of unindexed corank-one coverage remains.
residual_risks: A later or unpublished theorem resolving all singular graphs could subsume this special case, but none was identified in the inspected literature.
Graph real coefficients and rank n−1 assumptions are essential; no statement for higher nullity or arbitrary fields.

value.rationale: This gives a sharp rank-defect-one extension of an explicit unresolved singular-graph isomorphism problem, with a rigidity classification of every isomorphism and an exact higher-nullity counterexample. The unique false-twin support case is a natural algebraic boundary and requires argument beyond the standard 2LI condition; result is useful independent of the whole higher-nullity conjecture.
residual_risks: Value concerns the precisely stated natural object and invariant; the finding does not settle unclaimed broader classifications.
